divya.k: Heads-up — repro for a weird tokenization/emoji fold between qwen/gemma -> llama tokenizers after our int4 conversion. small failing perf/regression on chat-summarize eval.

matt: What do you mean by "emoji fold"? token ids changing?

divya.k: Yeah, short: sequences with ZWJ emoji (e.g. 👩‍💻) split differently. Gemma tokenizer outputs a single token id, llama tokenizer splits it into base+zwj+modifier. That changes offsets and we see generation diffs. quick dump below.

divya.k: ```
# gemma-tokenizer.encode('I love 👩‍💻') -> [101, 2057, 1920]  # (toy ids)
# llama-tokenizer.encode('I love 👩‍💻') -> [101, 2057, 500, 37, 1920]
# downstream: kv-cache alignment + prefix caching assumes same tokenization -> misaligned past keys
```

sara: That would definitely explain the quality drop. Did the conversion script change any normalization (NFC/NFKC) step? emoji ZWJ sequences are brittle.

divya.k: Conversion didn't touch unicode norm explicitly. We call sentencepiece/tokenizers libs as-is. But I noticed the gemma tokenizer has an internal pre-normalize step that folds emoji ligatures. The llama tokenizers we use are strict unicode-preserve.

jon: This matches the bench: chat-summarize v2 run (eval-run-id: eval-2026-03-18-19) shows -2.1% ROUGE-L for gemma-int4 compared to host baseline. Traces show start token offset mismatch on many examples with emoji or skin-tone modifiers.

convert-bot: model-conversion(gemma-lite-int4) finished: artifacts/conv/2026-03-18/gemma-lite-int4.tar.gz (no errors) :white_check_mark:

matt: Ok. Two short mitigation ideas: 1) canonicalize input to NFKC + emoji ZWJ normalization before tokenization (cheap, runtime). 2) add a conversion-time tokenmap sanity check: ensure token count parity for a small emoji-heavy probe set.

divya.k: I'll patch a quick canonicalizer in the tokenizer pipeline and re-run the eval sweep. also going to add the emoji probe to the conversion unit tests.

sara: For long-term, we should add a tokenmap compat report during model onboarding: list of representative unicode sequences and per-model tokenization diffs. Throw in a tiny KV-cache alignment test too.

divya.k: Agreed. Plan:
- add NFKC+ZWJ-normalize step (feature-flagged)
- conversion-time probe with ~300 emoji/zwj combos
- unit test that runs token->id parity check and fails conversion if >1% mismatch
- rerun eval and report.

matt: Sounds good. If that fixes the eval, roll out a quick hotfix for hosted routing to enable canonicalizer for newly onboarded models.

divya.k: I'll post results here when I have the rerun (ETA: 2 hours). tagging @matt @sara for visibility. :thumbsup:
